query: In Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs phase stability and why, with relevance to retaining desirable combinations of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries of the hypothesis, supporting prior evidence, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the grain boundary character distribution, which in turn affects the alloy's high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
generation.intervention: Introduction of grain boundary engineering through thermomechanical processing and subsequent heat treatment at optimized conditions
generation.conditions: High-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness tests
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary character distribution and its effect on phase stability
generation.mechanism: The grain boundary engineering will influence the grain boundary character distribution, leading to changes in the alloy's properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy with optimized grain boundary character distribution will exhibit improved high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness compared to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy without grain boundary engineering
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is bounded by the material system, operating conditions, and the specific grain boundary engineering method used.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of grain boundary engineering in improving the desired properties is uncertain and needs to be confirmed by supporting prior evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the alloy's properties with and without grain boundary engineering
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with grain boundary engineering does not exhibit improved properties compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

proposals.conditions: High-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness tests
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of coherent precipitates and their effect on grain boundary segregation
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis proposes that the phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the competition between the formation of coherent precipitates and grain boundary segregation, which in turn affects the alloy's high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness. The Co to Cr ratio adjustment will influence the precipitate formation and grain boundary segregation, leading to changes in the alloy's properties.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The alloy with the optimal Co to Cr ratio will exhibit improved high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness compared to the baseline alloy. The formation of coherent precipitates will enhance the alloy's strength and resistance to radiation damage, while the grain boundary segregation will improve the alloy's environmental resistance and cryogenic toughness.
